label: copy-phase input of x or 3 (sparse, context-dependent subset)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (97% of mass), and only when the fed-back input token is x (50% of mass) or 3 (37%); o (10%) and v/s make up most of the rest. It essentially never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on other tokens. The token gate is necessary but far from sufficient: only about 2% of copy-phase x/3 inputs activate it, so precision is very low (F1 0.04 despite mass recall 0.86). Which occurrences fire depends on context that I could not capture with a simple rule. It favours recall_idx 3-4 and recall_idx 1, and is weak at recall_idx 2. It also depends on the token being output next: for 3, outputs x/o/w/i; for x, outputs s/c/f/v/x. It is silent with outputs l/n/q/w/digits after x. Restricting by out_tok or recall_idx raised precision only to about 4-8% and cost a lot of recall. The strongest activations (~0.25) are x at the first copy step of L=3 sequences starting with x, and 3 followed by x at recall_idx 3-4 in L=9 sequences.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: x, 3, o, v, s, l; least: w, p, b, j) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: x, o, i, w; delimiter step: x, o; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, t=2, L=4 & t=5.
